name: Empire Green
lede: Empire Green is a dark, grey-leaning green tied to Napoleonic France, though Napoleon did not start the fashion.

sections.title: Green at the First Empire
sections.body:
Pastoureau writes that during the First Empire green was as fashionable for clothing as for furniture and decoration in France [1]. The Sèvres porcelain factory, famous for its blues under Louis XV, had to widen its palette and offer new greens [1]. Greens of that period were still fairly dark and paired with Pompeian reds and bright gold [1]. Military uniforms gave green a place it had never had before, and influenced the uniforms of neighboring and allied countries [1].

A persistent myth, which Pastoureau corrects, credits Napoleon with starting the style because green was his favorite color [1]. Pastoureau grants that Bonaparte liked green throughout his life, but says he did not cause its popularity across Europe [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #4E644D is a dark, muted grey-green, near [[dark-green]] and [[sap-green]] in the data [9]. The books describe the Empire palette in words, not hex values [1]. The concordance of 29 color books finds only four strong mentions of this name, so the article stays short rather than pad the record [9]. Screen colors are approximate, and the swatch is a reference value, not a measured pigment [9].
